newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles $776 mln assessment passes narrowly.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles $776 mln assessment passes narrowly.

text.p: A measure that will raise $776 million to improve Los Angeles city parks was narrowly approved by voters, election officials said Tuesday.

Measure K, which will tax property owners $776 million over 30 years for city projects, including park and recreational facilities, was approved by 50.19 percent of the vote, just over the required 50 percent.
According to the final results, which will be certified later Tuesday, 366,446 voters backed the measure versus 363,632 who voted against it.
The measure appeared on the November 5 ballot but had been too close to call, election officials said.
The funds raised will not be used to back bonds, according to officials who spearheaded the drive for Measure K.
